title: Uber launches Baidu’s driverless Apollo Go robotaxis in Dubai
source_used: scanx.trade (its text reads as the Uber and Baidu joint announcement; no other outlet found in the search)
key_facts: Uber and Baidu launched fully driverless Apollo Go robotaxis on Uber's platform in Dubai on Thursday, the first deployment under their multi-year partnership.
New Horizon Luxury Transport operates the fleet, which uses the sixth-generation RT6 vehicle carrying up to three passengers.
Service covers select areas of Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah; riders requesting UberX or Uber Comfort may be matched, or can choose the Autonomous option.
Apollo Go has operated in 28 cities, with over 350 million autonomous kilometres, including over 240 million fully driverless.
Uber says it has more than 30 AV partners and that all autonomous vehicles must follow its Safety Guidelines.
The page also carries older, unrelated text about an Uber keynote at a 10 Sep conference, which is not used.
quote_evidence: Uber and Baidu have initiated the first operational phase of their strategic partnership by launching fully driverless Apollo Go robotaxis in Dubai.
Dubai serves as the launchpad for scaling thousands of Apollo Go vehicles across Uber’s global network.
why_it_matters_hint: The first fully driverless robotaxis on Uber's network in the Gulf, and a test case for other cities.
event_date: 8 Oct 2026 (Thursday, Dubai time; feed 7 Oct 2026, 22:44 UTC)
